newsitem.title: ZAIRE: No sign of relief for refugees in Zaire village.
newsitem.headline: No sign of relief for refugees in Zaire village.

text.p: Thousands may die if no food is distributed in the next few days among Rwandan refugees trapped in squalor in the remote Zaire village of Tingi-Tingi, a medical workers said.

Up to 120,000 Rwandans have fled to Tingi-Tingi, many walking for more than a month and surviving on roots and leaves, after fighting broke out between Rwandan-backed rebels and Zairean troops in eastern Zaire in October.

"There is no food for the vast majority of the people. If there is no food distribution between now and Christmas, thousands will be dead," said a French medical worker with the charity Medecins Sans Frontieres (Doctors Without Borders).
"We try to help. There is a rudimentary health service on the ground," the worker told reporters who visited Tingi-Tingi at the weekend.
There is still no organised feeding at Tingi-Tingi by international relief agencies except for occasional supplies of high-nutrition biscuits by the U.N. Children's Fund (UNICEF).
There are no toilets and the only source of water is a nearby stream, clearly polluted by the teeming population of sickly people.
"A humanitarian catastrophe is in the making here," said Philippe Duamelle, West Africa coordinator of emergency programmes for UNICEF.
"Many children are suffering from malnutrition. There are 400 children in this centre and we are organising therapeutic feeding, but it's not reaching all the needy," he said.
Rebel advances in the east uprooted more than a million Hutu refugees who had fled to Zaire after civil war and massacre of up to a million Tutsis in Rwanda in 1994 by Hutu hardliners.
Most have returned home since last month, but many headed deeper into Zaire, fearing persecution if they returned home.
Those trapped in Tingi-Tingi, many of them young children, intended to reach Kisangani, the largest town in northeastern Zaire, about 500 km (300 miles) from the war zone.
The village is seven km (four miles) east of Lubutu, a town about halfway along the road to Kisingani from Zaire's eastern border with Rwanda and Burundi.
"The condition of refugees in Tingi-Tingi is deplorable," said Rwandan Maurice Niwese. "To get here some have walked 400 km (250 miles) without food, hungry and exhausted."

Refugee spokesman Serundada Innocent estimates there are around 120,000 refugees in Tingi-Tingi, barred access to Lubutu by Zairean authorities who do not want to see new refugee camps take root there, but aid workers are less precise.
"We ought to avoid getting into a quarrel about numbers. There could be 40,000, 50,000 or 100,000, it's difficult to say at the moment," UNICEF's Duamelle said.

"We're the ones who have been forgotten by the international community," Serundada told Reuters during an earlier visit last week. "It's the survival of the fittest. Those who can't reach Tingi-Tingi die on the way."
